passage.title: The Magic Seed
passage.text:
Ava planted a seed no bigger than a grain of rice, burying it two centimetres under the soil — deep enough to stay moist, but shallow enough for sunlight to eventually reach the sprout.

For five days, nothing appeared above the surface. Underground, though, the seed was absorbing water and splitting open as a root pushed downward and a shoot pushed up.

Once the shoot broke through the soil, growth sped up. Photosynthesis — using sunlight, water and air to make food — let the plant grow leaves, then a thick stem taller than Ava's father.

By late summer, a sunflower head opened at the top, packed with hundreds of seeds. A bee visited to collect nectar, brushing against the pollen and carrying some away to the next flower it landed on.
